assumptions: 1. THE CREATORS DECLARE NOTHING YET (VELDO-0302 is not built). The suite declares and confirms each worktree and each run directory itself, or adopts the worktree as reconcile would. The census finds the worktree's item by path. In production a worktree no item records gets no census and no folders (rows ac4/not-recorded, ac3/nothing-given).

2. NOTHING IN THE ENGINE BUILDS `space` YET (VELDO-0303's assumption 3). The receiver's main() passes none, so until a later ticket wires it a run is given what it was given before and no census runs. The suite wires the mapping itself.

3. THE RECEIVER IS MADE WITHOUT ITS STORES. object.__new__ and the attributes _space_given and _remove_run read; _engine_cwd answers the fixture worktree. The one spawn itself is not driven: that it gives the folders before the execution record and before any process start is read from its source (ac3/spawn-order), and the worker of ac3/declared-before-worker is a python process the row starts with the environment the receiver gave. Other stand-ins: the two checks of a switch to act (VELDO-0332, 0339), the docker client (a function), the process table (an empty fixture folder).

4. COMMITTED IS READ AS THE PROJECT'S, NOT THE RUN'S (review, finding 1). An ignore file covers a folder only when the commit the worktree's item records as its start holds it, the worktree's HEAD holds that content and so does the disk. A run that adds or changes a rule, committed or not, gets nothing from that whole file: its ignored folders stay as work, which costs space and loses nothing. A worktree with no recorded start commit gets declared patterns only. NOT CLOSED HERE: the start commit is the ledger's record, and a rebranch written after the run's commit would move it (the creators are VELDO-0302); a build output item declared before the run changed the ignore file stays an item; the remover's last look still asks only that git tracks the file (VELDO-0347).

5. RULE 5 DOES NOT READ IGNORED WORK YET (VELDO-0347 AC1). The census never records such a path, so nothing removes it as build output. That the worktree around it stays is shown at worktree abandoned in ac2/ignored-uncovered, where the keep step and the remover's last look hold it; the row asserts the worktree is not removed and the files are byte for byte, not the name of the deferral.

6. NOT BUILT HERE, by the ticket's criteria: the run's label and compose project name and the census of Docker objects (VELDO-0306); the order census, Signal, release with the conclusive end (VELDO-0308), so a run with no run directory gets its census at the receiver's end and no run finished from it; the gate's census at a verdict (VELDO-0309). A run in the confined runner and an engine on another host are given no folders (the spec's History says why).

7. THE NAMES AND THE REFUSALS ARE THIS TICKET'S CHOICE: <first build root>/<worktree name>-<digest of its path>, <first scratch root>/run-scratch/<digest of the dispatch>, unavailable_service:space_ledger for a ledger that refuses or cannot be reached, invalid_state:space_folder_unrecorded, invalid_state:space_folder_recorded_otherwise and invalid_state:space_folder_run_directory for a folder, and invalid_input:space_build_variable. The design fixes none of them. Only the first scratch root and the first build root are used. The folder's path is in the refusal's detail and in the receiver's refused event; the dispatch record holds the code only, because its refuse command has no detail field and control_dispatch.py is outside this footprint.

8. THE NEGATION READ IS WIDER THAN GIT'S, ON PURPOSE (review, finding 2). Every .gitignore on disk from the folder's directory to the top is read, committed or not; a star crosses a slash; a pattern with a backslash matches everything; a folder that cannot be walked is work. So a project with a negation such as !.gitkeep keeps as work every ignored folder that holds such a file, and each such folder is walked at each census. Negations in info/exclude and in ignore files inside the folder itself are not read: git does not read the second, and the first is a personal rule.
9. REVIEW FINDING 6 IS NOT FIXED HERE (a reused build root keeps its first run as owner; build output, so no work is lost), by the lead's scope for this fix. The review's notes stand as written.

10. NEGATIONS ARE READ WIDER THAN GIT READS THEM (re-review, finding 2-b). A negation pattern in a .gitignore above the folder, in the repository's info/exclude or in a .gitignore inside the folder makes the folder work when it could match the folder or a path in it; the match lets a star cross a slash and tries a pattern with no slash on every name in the folder, so some real build output stays on disk as work: space, never loss. NOT CLOSED HERE: a negation in a personal excludes file that core.excludesFile names is not read (that file is never read); finding 6 of the review (a reused build root keeps its first run as owner; build output, no work lost) stays deferred; the re-review's note 1 (the recorded start commit must be one the project landed, never a run branch's tip) is for the writer of those records. The re-review's finding 7 was closed by VELDO-0306's own commits: template sync passes and suites 133 to 141 are green on this tree.
rollback: Revert the change. Runs leave build output with no record.
